methodology.displayName: Reciprocal trade additionality and completion model v1

estimandDefinitions.success_case_additional: The counterparty resource or action that would occur if the accepted reciprocal agreement is completed, excluding the participant’s own commitment and excluding any quantity present in the counterparty’s frozen no-agreement baseline.
estimandDefinitions.expected_additional: The success-case additional quantity multiplied by the modeled probability that the counterparty completes because of the agreement rather than under the frozen no-agreement baseline.
estimandDefinitions.direct_causal_attribution: The verified counterparty quantity attributable to the participant under the approved role-specific completion and baseline-credibility model, capped at the verified counterparty quantity.
estimandDefinitions.verified_additional: The independently verified counterparty resource or action absent from the frozen baseline, recorded only after the agreement’s evidence and review requirements are final.

methodology.baselineDefinition: Before either party accepts, freeze each party’s concrete no-agreement plan, quantity, timing, destination, evidence standard, confidence in that plan, and any already-scheduled overlapping action. A later claim cannot increase additionality unless it is supported by contemporaneous evidence that predates acceptance.
methodology.algorithmDescription: Read the participant-scoped frozen terms and baseline. Compute the deterministic success-case quantity from the counterparty commitment after removing baseline and overlapping quantities. Estimate joint completion and baseline credibility from the narrowest healthy hierarchical reference class. Multiply the success-case quantity by the modeled causal completion probability for expected additionality. After final evidence, cap direct causal attribution at verified additional quantity; never infer additionality from a receipt alone.

referenceClassPolicy.uncertaintyExpansionRule: At each broadening step, add between-class variance to the predictive distribution and expand the 80% interval. Withhold if no class meets the minimum or if baseline-credibility calibration is unavailable.

uncertaintyPolicy.method: Use a calibrated hierarchical beta-binomial model for completion and a separately calibrated baseline-credibility model; propagate both distributions by posterior simulation into the native-unit estimate.
uncertaintyPolicy.confidencePolicy: Withhold when model health is blocked or stale. Label low confidence only after health passes and the eligible sample is at least 50; moderate requires at least 100 eligible resolved observations, no more than one approved reference-class broadening step, and no blocking calibration failure; high requires at least 200 observations, the narrowest approved class, empirical 80% coverage between 75% and 85%, calibration slope between 0.8 and 1.2, and no active warnings.

requiredCalibrationMetrics: Brier score for modeled completion or activation probability
blockedConditions: eligible resolved-observation count below the methodology minimum
80% interval empirical coverage outside the approved tolerance
required state is missing or does not match the immutable state hash
input is outside the approved domain
unresolved evidence-integrity, duplication, or overlap failure
baseline data unavailable for either party
same verified quantity would be additively attributed to more than one participant
warningConditions: reference class broadened beyond the narrowest approved class
sample size below the high-confidence threshold
calibration drift within the warning band
material share of observations relies on participant attestation rather than independent evidence
counterfactual baseline supported only by self-attestation
participant pair has prior repeated agreements outside the reference class

sourceDataRequirements: immutable accepted agreement terms and participant roles
both pre-acceptance no-agreement baselines with timestamps
private evidence and review outcome references
cancellation, dispute, amendment, and completion lifecycle history
deduplication keys for overlapping platform and off-platform actions
knownFailureModes: strategic understatement of the no-agreement baseline
receipt proves occurrence but not causation
agreement amendments invalidate the state hash
the same resource is claimed by both participants or another mechanism
completion evidence omits material quality or timing differences
outOfDomainConditions: unbounded, illegal, coercive, deceptive, or unverifiable commitment
no concrete pre-acceptance baseline for either party
commitment quantity cannot be represented in a stable native unit
more than two substantive counterparties without an approved coalition model
material third-party harm or benefit is known but not represented in the frozen terms
materialChangeTriggers: reference-class fields, broadening order, or minimum sample size changes
probability, uncertainty, or confidence method changes
new data source or evidence-quality tier
aggregation, overlap, or double-counting rule changes
new participant role or lifecycle state
change from counterparty-resource attribution to total-agreement attribution

aggregationPolicy.overlapHandling: A verified resource, action, signer, or deliverable may appear in multiple explanatory views, but may enter an additive platform aggregate at most once. Direct causal attribution and cooperative allocation are alternative attribution lenses and are never summed. Currency, count, duration, and value-adjusted quantities remain separate unless an independently approved immutable conversion snapshot exists.

parameters.publicationRule: withhold modeled components unless exact-hash model approval and current health pass exist
